memo.verdict: Neutral; park; medium conviction. Neste (NESTE-FI) at 31.93 EUR (close 2026-10-06) is a cyclical margin recovery with a self-help overlay and a regulatory demand step beneath it, and the shares already pay for the recovery and the self-help. The modal return is 15.6 percent a year over eighteen months (to 2028-04-07, value including cash returns 39.65 EUR) and 11.0 percent a year over three years (to 2029-10-07, 43.70 EUR), below the 20 percent bar at both horizons; on the probability-weighted multiple of 12.6x it is 8.0 and 7.4 percent a year. The park is on the return and the riskiness, not on the gate: management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability A, no D or F. Re-open on: the Q3 report on 2026-10-29 with a renewable margin at or above USD 1,100 a tonne and utilisation at or above 80 percent, followed by a 2027 contract round reported at or above USD 1,000 a tonne and a dated Rotterdam milestone (FY2027 EPS toward 3.0 EUR, eighteen-month return toward 20 percent a year); or a price at or below 30 EUR with the modal path intact (the eighteen-month clearing level, 30.2 EUR), or at or below 25 EUR for the three-year case (25.3 EUR). Toward invalidation: a Q3 margin below USD 1,000 a tonne with the spot proxy below USD 800; a renewable margin below USD 700 a tonne persistently; no Rotterdam start-up in 2027 or capex above EUR 2,500m.
case: - The change is real, broad and finished travelling the chain. A new chief executive and CFO chose retrenchment and delivered it: EUR 594m against EUR 350m, hydrogen project cancelled, 510 positions cut, leverage from 37.8 to 29.9 percent. The outputs followed (USD 1,223 a tonne; USD 25.8 a barrel; comparable EBITDA EUR 1,203m in Q2 2026; FY2026 consensus EPS up 350 percent to 3.77 EUR). There is no layer left to reach.

- The strongest force on the outputs is external and transient. About 40 percent of the Q2 2026 margin expansion came from the distillate squeeze after the Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz closure; a ceasefire was negotiated at the end of Q2 2026; brokers assume Porvoo's margin normalises to a real USD 12 a barrel by 2028. The internal change explains perhaps EUR 594m of a EUR 2,500m rise in EBITDA.

- The demand step is a floor on volume, not on margin. German double-counting abolished from January 2026 (1.5 million tonnes); US obligations 8.86 billion RINs for 2026; renewable diesel demand from 19 to over 30 million tonnes by 2030, SAF from 2 to 7 million. Capacity of the same order arrives in 2027 to 2028: Rotterdam, Enilive (Livorno 500,000 tonnes by end-2026; Priolo by 2028), Repsol (1.5 million tonnes by 2028), US plants above nameplate (DGD 1.20 billion gallons; Rodeo targeting 800 million), up to 3 million tonnes of potential Chinese SAF with no duty (EU duties of 21.7 to 35.6 percent cover biodiesel only). The 2024 trough at USD 242 a tonne with the same mandates in prospect shows the margin can fall far below USD 800.
counter_case: - The bull's case at full force: the market is mispricing a structural step-change as a cyclical peak. RED III, the German physical step of 1.5 million tonnes, Spain from 2027, the EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese biodiesel and the ReFuelEU ramp put a mandate floor under European renewable margins near USD 1,000 a tonne, not 800; the majors have cancelled their European projects (Shell Rotterdam halted September 2025; BP selling Gelsenkirchen; CVR reverting Wynnewood); Neste's pretreatment moat lets it run the cheapest feedstock in the tightest market; Rotterdam adds 24 percent to volume into that floor from 2027. At USD 1,000 a tonne and Rotterdam volumes FY2028 EPS is about 3.4 EUR, the April 2028 24-month-forward figure about 3.6 EUR, 50 EUR at 14.0x plus dividends (38 percent a year) and 60 EUR at the 16.8x the stock last carried as a grower (38 to 55 percent a year). Rothschild & Co Redburn (the valuation "embeds little credit for a structurally higher margin base"), DNB Carnegie (margins "persist longer than consensus expects"; a 40 EUR target; the multiple "well below its fifteen-year average of 16x to 18x") and Jefferies (enterprise value below asset replacement cost; 39 EUR; the post-results fall overdone) hold it, as do the brokers at 3.6 to 3.9 EUR of FY2027 EPS (Goldman Sachs, Texas Capital, TPH). The market has been wrong on Neste in both directions inside two years (consensus target 12.23 EUR in early 2025, 40 EUR by September 2026).

- Conceded: the mandate floor is real, physical and in force; the 2027 contract round is being struck in Q4 2026 against a spot of USD 1,000 a tonne or more; a drawdown to 25 EUR with the margin at USD 800 would make the case a B at eighteen months on the record's own arithmetic; if the margin resolves toward USD 1,000 the modal path and the 'Investment Thesis' rating are wrong by a Building Block.
triggers: - The renewable margin in 2027: whether the FY2027 comparable sales margin holds at or above USD 800 a tonne (modal USD 900; consensus implies about USD 975). Toward the bull: a Q4 2026 contract round reported at or above USD 1,000 a tonne. Toward the bear: a Q3 margin below USD 1,000 with the spot proxy below USD 800. Alarm below USD 800 in a quarter; invalidate below USD 700 persistently (Morgan Stanley's trigger USD 700; DNB Carnegie's USD 500).

- Rotterdam: whether commercial start-up falls within 2027 and 2028 volumes reach about 1.0 million tonnes; a dated mechanical-completion milestone in the Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 report, or its absence. A slip to 2028 takes 2028 EPS down about 0.4 EUR and the multiple to 12.5x. Alarm a dated slip into 2028; invalidate capex above EUR 2,500m or no start-up in 2027.

- The crack: whether Oil Products' margin normalises from USD 25.8 a barrel toward a real USD 12 by 2028 (probable, in the path and consensus); a crack above USD 20 a barrel through 2027 adds about 0.5 EUR to FY2027 EPS and moves the eighteen-month return into the B band. Alarm below USD 12 in a quarter before Rotterdam contributes.
- The re-rating: whether the market pays 14.0x by April 2028; needs the floor and the volume leg together; either alone is 12.5x or 11.0x.
- Utilisation: the reading after the Singapore turnaround (from December 2026); alarm below 80 percent for two quarters; invalidate below 75 percent for two quarters after the turnarounds.

- Policy: a second European mandate cut on affordability (alarm); a rollback of the German step or RED III transposition (invalidate); EU SAF targets for 2026 to 2029; EU trade defence on Chinese SAF; LCFS credits below USD 50 a tonne.
